teaser.text: Xiaomi Corporation is a Chinese company that sells smartphones, connected household products and electric cars. It also earns money from the software, advertising, games, finance and support services that grow around those products, so its business is a flow of sales, costs, cash and customer relationships.

blocks.heading: Where could Xiaomi's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is HKD3.01 in October 2027, a return of -89% including dividends, and HKD3.57 in October 2029, a return of -86%. It assigns 30% probability to the bear case, 50% to the base case and 20% to the bull case. Even the October 2029 bull price is HKD4.95, a return of -81%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Xiaomi?

paragraphs.text: The bear case uses revenue of CNY470 billion, CNY480 billion and CNY500 billion, with margins of 3.2%, 3.0% and 3.2%. Smartphone margin had fallen to 8.5% in the June quarter, while the combined EV, AI and new-initiatives segment reported a CNY5.7 billion first-half operating loss. The bull case uses CNY530 billion, CNY620 billion and CNY720 billion of revenue, with margins rising from 7.0% to 9.0%. That requires vehicle scale, stable phone economics and continued high-margin service growth. Internet services had a 76.5% gross margin in 2025.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Xiaomi really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash from operations after capital spending, lease payments and interest paid. It fell in 2025 even as revenue and reported earnings rose. The free-cash-flow margin narrowed from 7.9% to 3.9%, so less of each sales yuan remained after the business funded itself.

Employee share pay adds another economic cost. It does not consume cash when recorded, but it compensates employees and can dilute shareholders. A specialist therefore keeps actual capital spending in free cash flow and considers stock compensation separately.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Xiaomi today?

paragraphs.text: The P/E ratio compares a share price with annual earnings per share. A price of HK$26.38 divided by earnings of HK$1.46 produces a P/E of 18.1 times. P/E can rise even while a share falls if profit falls faster: Xiaomi earned about RMB2.5 billion in 2022, after RMB19.3 billion the year before.

earnings.title: Xiaomi earnings: results and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Xiaomi's next results are expected on November 24, 2026; guidance centers on EV deliveries, AI and R&D, while margins and cash remain key.
earnings.opening: Xiaomi's next results are expected on November 24, 2026. Watch whether new-car orders become cash-generating deliveries.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Xiaomi's business works, who its rivals are, how management operates, and what risks it faces.

paragraphs.text: Xiaomi targets 550,000 smart-EV deliveries in the year to December 2026. July deliveries were 31,267, while the first seven months totalled 216,322. That leaves nearly 67,000 deliveries a month for the final five months, more than twice July’s pace.

Management expects to invest RMB16,000 million in AI during 2026 and more than RMB200 billion in R&D from 2026 to 2030. That implies average annual R&D spending above RMB40 billion, though Xiaomi has not promised an even schedule. Management has also said it has not changed its R&D direction.

blocks.heading: Has Xiaomi kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Xiaomi has also kept a concrete customer promise. Its hardware net profit margin should not exceed 5%, with excess returned to users. The reported margin for 2025 was 2.3%. That means about RMB2.30 remained as profit for every RMB100 of hardware revenue under Xiaomi’s definition. It is an overall business result, not a markup on every product. The promise may build customer trust, but it deliberately limits direct hardware profitability.

blocks.heading: What do Xiaomi's last eight reported periods show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue was down 6.1% from the year-earlier quarter but up 9.9% sequentially. Gross margin fell to 19.8%, and operating income and shareholder net income also declined year on year. The sequential rebound therefore did not restore the earlier profitability.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Xiaomi's next results?

paragraphs.text: October–December deliveries will reveal whether September’s improvement became a sustained ramp. Sky Nomad had more than 70,000 locked-in orders by October 8, but orders still require production, inspection, transport, payment and service. Watch conversion and cancellations alongside output: extra capacity cannot repair weak demand, while strong demand cannot eliminate a factory bottleneck.
